# BOOK 1 of 2: The Crow's Inn Tragedy (Annie Haynes, 1927)

## Ch I – Crow's Inn, Bechcombe & Turner's office
- Offices of Messrs. Bechcombe & Turner, first floor of corner house, Crow's Inn Square (No. 21). Old, grimy firm; no lifts.
- Rev. James Collyer (tall, grey-haired clergyman, rector of Wexbridge; kind grey eyes, worn face) calls on brother-in-law **Luke Bechcombe** (solicitor, small, spare, grey beard, horn-rimmed spectacles, thinning grey hair; sole head since partner Turner retired to Streatham villa).
- Collyer's wife (Mrs. Collyer, Luke's sister) is an invalid, wounded/gassed son **Tony (Anthony) Collyer** came back from WWI prison camp, drifts between jobs, debts paid 3 times by father. Tony offered post as bear-leader to younger brother of friend (a "defective" lad).
- Tony is in love with **Cecily Hoyle**, Luke's secretary (nice, typist/shorthand, "nothing particular" looks; engaged by Mrs. Madeline Bechcombe).
- Luke gossips: **Aubrey Todmarsh** (Collyer's nephew; conscientious objector; runs East End settlement; after money; engaged/expected to marry rich American widow **Mrs. Phillimore**, who finances his schemes). Luke dislikes Aubrey; Luke dislikes League of Nations.
- Collyer needs money; family **emerald cross** (Collyer heirloom, kept in secret drawer of writing-table). Luke says emeralds are **paste**. Luke will sell them; Collyer gave them to him (in old leather case). Warned re **the Yellow Gang / "Yellow Dog"** thieves.
- Luke's typewriter-clicking secretary in side room; no communicating door.

## Ch II – South London Settlement of Confraternity of St. Philip
- Settlement by river, South London; uniforms: dark blue serge coats, blue bone buttons, white overalls.
- Door-man (short, coal-black hair, white face, fish-like mouth) admits Collyer; Aubrey Todmarsh greets him. Aubrey: thin, overjowled, dark sleek hair, "visionary" look.
- Protégé **Michael Farmore** (ex-burglar) arrested attempting to break into General Craven's house, Mortimer Square.
- Tony arrives with **Hopkins** (Aubrey's right-hand man; "phiz" like Madame Tussaud's Chamber of Horrors). Tony takes father to pub for lunch. Mrs. Phillimore seen in car with two men near laundry.
- Collyer tells Aubrey of paste emeralds. Aubrey warns against naming names.

## Ch III – Bank messenger / Luke's death (Friday, 12 noon)
- Luke tells managing clerk **Amos Thompson** (thin, reddish-grey beard, sunken grey eyes, horn-rimmed smoke glasses, missing front teeth, stooped; 18 years with firm) no one to disturb him until 1 pm; appointments Mr. Geary and Mr. Pound (last at 11.45). Bank messenger expected.
- Tony at noon demands to see uncle; Thompson refuses; Tony says he will go to private door. Knocking heard twice.
- Clerks: **Percy Johnson** (articled pupil), **John Walls** (second in command, florid), **William Spencer** (junior, jaunty), Brunton (office boy later).
- Walls and Spencer look through keyhole, see body by window. Rugby-player articled pupil breaks door. Luke Bechcombe strangled, chloroformed (sweet smell). Doctor (rooms nearby) says dead ~2 hrs; "Strangled!"
- **Cecily Hoyle** (tall, thin, clear brown eyes, turned-up nose, wide mouth, nut-brown curly hair) present.

## Ch IV – Inquest-style interviews, Inspector Furnival
- **Inspector Furnival** ("The Ferret," Scotland Yard, foxy face, sharp grey eyes; scratches nose with pen handle). **Dr. Hackett** (large-featured) gives death ~12 noon, chloroform, strangulation.
- Furnival examines Walls (Thompson missing since 12.30), Spencer (saw a tall woman with bright yellow hair, powder, long white suède glove on stairs ~12.30), Cecily.
- White **suède glove** found beside writing-table.
- Cecily: saw Luke ~11.45 (he gave her lunch leave; he rang bell); went to lunch with Tony; they were called back by Luke ("I want you, Tony"); she waited in **St. Philip's Field of Rest** (old graveyard behind St. Philip's church) — Tony arrived ~20–30 min later; she returned ~1.30. Heard Luke moving about after 1.30 (chair scraping). She gives Hobart Residence, Windover Square (girls' club) as address; father "Mr. Hoyle" artist, abroad.
- Rector Collyer arrives; Tony was at office; Luke dined with Collyers night before at Carlsford Square.

## Ch V – Carlsford Square dining room
- Aubrey, Tony, Collyer, Mrs. Madeline Bechcombe (regal, aquiline, dark eyes), cousin barrister **John Steadman** (K.C.-type criminologist, short, undistinguished).
- Tony: says he went to the office, saw Uncle Luke, who wanted him to come see him that night. Tony's account: uncle kept him minutes; he missed the Field of Rest ~half-hour.
- Mrs. Bechcombe: believes a woman (with glove) killed Luke.
- Steadman visits Furnival: Thompson's disappearance; Thompson address found in Luke's book → **10 Brooklyn Terrace, North Kensington**.

## Ch VI – Brooklyn Terrace
- Room at top of No. 10: oak table, 3 chairs, bed with flock mattress, corner cupboard; nothing else. Postcard of Cecily (amateur snapshot, from the Field of Rest). Detective novel from library. Old slippers.
- Landlord (first floor) reports Thompson paid rent Saturday mornings, four years.
- Library (Notting Hill Gate): Thompson borrowed books; manager describes him (brown beard, missing teeth, horn-rimmed glasses).

## Ch VII – Fraud revealed; Hopkins sighting
- Auditors: Thompson defalcations; Tony and Aubrey quarrel (Aubrey claims guilt of "lust for killing"); Tony says he has "some more money when Aunt Madeline dies."
- Fingerprints: rubber gloves. Chloroform. Furnival thinks woman's fingers too large for glove.
- Aubrey: Hopkins saw Thompson-like man at docks with manicured hands, going on cargo boat.
- Phone: "lady" at Scotland Yard, saw Luke on day of death.

## Ch VIII – Mrs. Cyril B. Carnthwacke
- American millionaire **Cyril B. Carnthwacke**; wife **Bella Laymond** (former Variety stage). She gambled, blackmailed by ex-lover; planned to sell diamonds substituting paste; sought Luke's help through phone.
- Appointment 12.15 (arrived ~12.30); Luke gave her receipt: "Mrs. Carnthwacke has entrusted her diamonds to me ... Signed Luke Francis Bechcombe." Diamonds locked in cupboard (not real safe); cupboard found empty. She says Luke alive at ~12.30; receipt stamped "One o'clock" (her story).
- Carnthwacke's maid's knowledge; fortune-teller "Fédora" (Madame Fédora) heard by Mrs. C.

## Ch IX – Hobart Residence; Hoyle address; Burford
- Cecily's temp address Miss Cochrane, Morley House, Beesford, Meadshire.
- Inspector: picture postcard; torn telegram: "Do not mention home address. Father." handed in Edgware Road 12.30, March 4th; letter fragment "5 o'clock, Physical Energy" (Kensington Gardens statue).
- Time-table at Cecily's desk: Burford, New Forest underlined.
- Steadman & Furnival plan Burford trip.

## Ch X – Burford; Rose Cottage
- "Royal Arms" inn; landlord; Mr. Hoyle of Rose Cottage, artist, sidesman, away sketching; housekeeper **Mrs. Wye**. Steadman sees water-colours signed "Christopher Hoyle" painted over other signatures; different hands. Burglaries: Squire Morpeth (Park), Sir John Lington (Lillinghurst).

## Ch XI – Kensington Gardens; Tony & Cecily; Steadman
- Cecily says it's over; reveals (whispers) something; begs Tony not to investigate. Steadman meets Tony, offers post with invalid young Bramley at **Bramley Hall**, near Burford (New Forest). Burglary there ~18 months earlier (Yellow Gang).

## Ch XII – Mr. Cyril B. Carnthwacke at Scotland Yard
- Carnthwacke: white glove; wife's diamonds; receipt. Suspects Thompson & Bechcombe in-cahoots. Fortune-teller Fédora. Luke's face unmarked.

## Ch XIII – Tube station; Hopkins arrested
- Anthony sees Cecily with man (Burford talk); Furnival with Tony going to Mrs. Luke Bechcombe's (family party for Aubrey–Mrs. Phillimore engagement).
- Steadman's arm injured by Mrs. Phillimore's chauffeur; child (Hopkins's) under car.
- Aubrey: Hopkins arrested at **Whistone Hall** (Sir Thomas Wreford) in New Forest, burglary; held at Burchester.

## Ch XIV – Carnthwackes' revelation
- Mrs. C. shown portrait: man not Luke Bechcombe; wrong hair, beard, build. Carnthwacke: murderer impersonated Luke.
- Mrs. Phillimore: "Sadie," "Butterfly"; says Mrs. C. not telling all.

## Ch XV–XVI – Emeralds; Aubrey's blotter; Collyer destroys
- Police found emeralds (Collyer identifies uncertainly).
- Aubrey's hand cut (penknife); Collyer mops blood on blotter; finds note in blotter (Mrs. C at Crow's Inn with the twinklers at quarter to twelve); burns it. Collyer leaves in drunk-seeming state.

## Ch XVII – Brunton's evidence; Yellow Gang meeting
- Brunton: fog, heard Thompson and woman (Cecily-like voice): "you must shake them off..."
- Note: "Wednesday night, 21 Burlase Street, Limehouse. Chink-a-pin."

## Ch XVIII – Cecily at Burford; flight
- Cecily goes to Burford, meets Mrs. Wye; takes envelope "11260" from father's (Hoyle's) desk. Old beggar follows; tunnel train incident (doctor and Masterman, detective disguised). Masterman: "Samuel Horsingforth, Sta. Irica, Portugal."

## Ch XIX – Mrs. Carnthwacke assaulted; Steadman
- Mrs. C strangled in carriage (Victoria Gate, Hyde Park); "dying"; she says assailant had long thumb, short index finger; Carnthwacke's house Blanden Square.

## Ch XX – Thompson arrested at Southampton
- "Samuel Horsingforth" passenger on *Atlantic*; arrested by Furnival. Alias John Frederick Hoyle; Thompson = Hoyle; Cecily is adopted daughter. Mrs. C reported dead (stop press).

## Ch XXI – Disguise; Yellow Dog trap
- Soho make-up shop; Steadman and Furnival disguised, yellow dominoes, go to Burlase-type house near Stepney; trapped in "Golden Room"; the Yellow Dog (stripped, bound).

## Ch XXII–XXIII – Escape; fire
- Naked, bound; knife under door, note (window to river). Escape by river; police launch. House raided; smoke/fire.

## Ch XXIV – Arrest of Aubrey Todmarsh
- Hopkins's return (wife Mrs. Hopkins). Aubrey arrested as Yellow Dog: "Aubrey William Todmarsh, alias the Yellow Dog ... wilful murder of Luke Bechcombe ... February 3rd." Poison (cyanide) substituted by tabloid powder.
- Tony and Cecily reconcile at Bechcombe House; Cecily is Dr. James Hoyle's daughter (mother's child).

END OF BOOK 1.

# BOOK 2 of 2: The Spring Song (Forrest Reid, 1916)

## Setting & main characters
- Summer, June; Canon Annesley's glebe house (Wexbridge-like village, Ballinreagh church). Grandpapa = Canon Annesley (white fluffy hair, red face, writing book on fairies; organist Mr. Clement Bradley).
- Aunt Caroline (Annesley, tall, fair, smiling, letter-writer).
- Miss Johnson (governess; pince-nez; writing novel *Be True, Fond Heart*; hero Reginald; Mr. Drummond the curate).
- Children: **Grif (Griffith) Weston** (13; sensitive, quiet, sleepy; sleepwalker; plays flute-tune dreams; dog Pouncer); **Jim** (9, sailor suit, scout); **Barbara** (12, priggish); **Ann** (10, fat, freckled, "Angelina"); **Edward** (15, fair, blue eyes; calls Palmer "Angelina"?—Edward is called Angelina at school); **Palmer Dorset** (red hair, freckled, small reddish-brown eyes; detective-minded; pater a doctor).
- Pouncer (bulldog, Grif's dog; Ann says "Bouncer").
- Miss Johnson's birthday; Doctor O'Neill (broad, bachelor, 30s).
- Captain Narcissus Batt, sisters Miss Nancy and Miss Jane; grandson Billy Tremaine (d. ~4 years, aged 14); flute belongs to Billy. House red brick, pond, cedars.
- Clement Bradley (real name Tennant; silver hair, ebony stick, shadow-obsession, killed a man on a bridge; in asylum).
- Pan and Syrinx (stable cats); tabby cat at Batt's gooseberry garden.

## Sequence of events
1. Arrival by train; Grif sleepy; Aunt Caroline meets them; walk in lane; Mr. Bradley introduced ("organist"). Grif chooses room overlooking wood.
2. Edward & Palmer arrive; Edward calls Palmer "Dorset"; Palmer's nickname "Angelina" for Edward (Ann's name slip). Jim's riddle "bun". Dinner; canon: riddles.
3. Croquet tournament; Grif sees Mr. Bradley playing; night window; flute heard.
4. Grif finds garden door; Batt house; lunch; raspberry wine; Billy's flute; Batts' tea.
5. Church: Bradley; ghost story (Bradley saw Billy in church, Spring Song by Gian Peruzzi); singing lesson.
6. Miss Johnson's visit suspicion; Daniel & lion (Pouncer bites Johnnie). Play "Be True Fond Heart" performed (Palmer, Ann Angelina, Edward Capt De Lancy, Jim Maud, Barbara). Miss Johnson offended.
7. Circus passes; Pouncer stolen by "George" (earring-man; Prairie Dick/Lascar); Grif chases circus, lost, sleeps in copse; dogs freed; sleeps in private wood.
8. Palmer and Edward stake out tool-shed; George shot in leg by Palmer's revolver (from saddler); Canon's life-preserver.
9. Grif found at dawn in river; Dragonfly; flute tune; returns to Batts.
10. Grif reads Tobit in churchyard; Palmer spying at Bradley's; Bradley: "ghost"; warns Grif of "dead" playmate.
11. Grif sleepwalks to Bradley's room; Palmer lets him in; Palmer: Bradley's real name Tennant.
12. Grif sends note via Jim; Bradley's shadow story; Grif falls ill ("Spring Song").
13. Doctor O'Neill & Palmer at Bradley's lodgings; revolver gift; Bradley's landlady; blotter; Bradley's signature "Clement Bradley Tennant".
14. Church fire: Bradley plays organ, sets fire; leaps from tower; dies. Doctor breaks window, can't enter.
15. Aftermath: Bradley's history revealed (homicide, asylum).
16. Grif recovers, visits Miss Nancy; Billy's room; Grif sleeps in Nancy's arms; ends "Grif falls asleep."
